advances: Ordinary full-dimensional volume and convex functions on simplex facets. The bound applies to affine halfspaces with arbitrary thresholds within the stated margin tolerance.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
**Weighted strip.** On a $k$-simplex the uniform barycentric coordinate $t$ has density $k(1-t)^{k-1}$ on $[0,1]$, since the opposite sections scale by $(1-t)^{k-1}$ and the density integrates to one. At fixed $t$ the remaining coordinates are $(1-t)W$, with $W$ uniform on the opposite $(k-1)$-simplex. This is a point when $k=1$. Put $A(t)=\mathbb E_W f(t,(1-t)W)$ in barycentric coordinates and $M=\int_F f\,d\mu_F$. The conditional average $A$ is convex and nonnegative, since its argument for each $W$ is affine in $t$. Moreover $M=\int_0^1 k(1-s)^{k-1}A(s)\,ds$.

If $|t-b|\le r$, the interval $[t-r,t+r]$ lies in $(0,1)$. Jensen's inequality on this interval and the lower bound $k(1-t-r)^{k-1}$ on the density give
$$
k(1-t)^{k-1}A(t)
\le \frac{M}{2r}\left(1-\frac{r}{1-t}\right)^{-(k-1)}
\le \frac{M}{r}.
$$
For the last step, $1-t\ge 1-b-r$ and $r\le(1-b)/(4k)$ give $r/(1-t)\le 1/(4k-1)$. Bernoulli's inequality gives $(1-r/(1-t))^{k-1}\ge1-(k-1)/(4k-1)>1/2$, also for $k=1$. Integrate over $|t-b|\le\eta$ to obtain the strip bound.

**Radial loss.** Let $\rho$ be the Minkowski gauge of $K-g$, with $\rho(v)=\inf\{a>0:v\in a(K-g)\}$. The inner simplex contains $g$ in its interior, so the gauge is finite. It is positively homogeneous and subadditive by convexity of $K-g$. If $K-g$ contains a ball of radius $\epsilon>0$ about zero, subadditivity and $\rho(v)\le |v|/\epsilon$ show continuity. On the facet $F_j=\{\lambda_j=0\}\cap S$ set $f_j(z)=\rho(z-g)-1$ and $w_j(z)=1-\rho(z-g)^{-d}$. The inclusions give $1\le \rho(z-g)\le(1-\delta)^{-1}$, so each $f_j$ is continuous, convex and nonnegative. The exact identity
$$
w_j(z)=f_j(z)\sum_{a=1}^d\rho(z-g)^{-a}
$$
gives $d(1-\delta)^d f_j(z)\le w_j(z)\le d f_j(z)$, including when $f_j(z)=0$.

The cones $\operatorname{conv}(g,F_j)$ partition $S$ up to null interfaces and each has volume $|S|/m$, since its volume ratio to $S$ equals $\lambda_j(g)=1/m$. On a cone the map $(a,z)\mapsto g+a(z-g)$ has Jacobian $a^{d-1}\operatorname{dist}(g,\operatorname{aff}F_j)$ relative to $da$ and facet area. Thus uniform probability in the cone has independent uniform $z$ on $F_j$ and radial parameter $a$ with density $d\cdot a^{d-1}$ on $[0,1]$. The part outside $K$ on this ray has $a>\rho(z-g)^{-1}$. For measurable $E\subset F_j$ the deleted volume over directions in $E$ is $(|S|/m)\int_E w_j\,d\mu_{F_j}$. In particular $\tau=m^{-1}\sum_j\int_{F_j}w_j\,d\mu_{F_j}$.

Any point of $H\mathbin{\triangle}C_i$ in $S$ satisfies $|\lambda_i(x)-b|\le\eta$. For a missing point written $x=g+a(z-g)$, one has $a\ge1-\delta$ and $\lambda_i(x)-b=a(\lambda_i(z)-b)$. Its endpoint therefore belongs to the strip $|\lambda_i(z)-b|\le\eta/(1-\delta)$. On $F_i$ this strip is empty, since $\lambda_i=0$ there and its width is at most $1/(4m)<b$. On $F_j$ for $j\ne i$, $\lambda_i$ is a facet barycentric coordinate. The strip estimate with $k=d-1$, $b=1/m$ has $r=1/(4m)$ and coefficient $2/r=8m$. Apply it to $f_j$ and use both radial weight comparisons to obtain
$$
\int_{\{|\lambda_i-b|\le\eta/(1-\delta)\}}w_j\,d\mu_{F_j}
\le 8m\eta(1-\delta)^{-d-1}\int_{F_j}w_j\,d\mu_{F_j}.
$$
Multiply by the cone volume fraction $1/m$ and sum over $j$. This proves the symmetric-difference bound, and adding the canonical loss bounds the missing volume in $H$.
statement:
Let $F$ be a $k$-dimensional simplex, $k\ge1$, with normalized volume $\mu_F$, and let $t$ be one of its barycentric coordinates. For $b\in(0,1)$ put $r=\frac14\min\{b,(1-b)/k\}$. Every continuous nonnegative convex function $f$ on $F$ satisfies
$$
\int_{\{|t-b|\le\eta\}} f\,d\mu_F
\le \frac{2\eta}{r}\int_F f\,d\mu_F,\qquad 0\le\eta\le r.
$$

Let $S$ be a full-dimensional simplex in $\mathbb R^d$, $d\ge2$, with centroid $g$ and barycentric functions $\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$. Put $m=d+1$, $b=1/m$, and $C_i=\{x:\lambda_i(x)\ge b\}$. Suppose $K$ is a compact convex body with $g+(1-\delta)(S-g)\subseteq K\subseteq S$ for $0\le\delta<1$. Write $\tau=1-|K|/|S|$ and $R_i=|(S\setminus K)\cap C_i|/|S|$, where $|\cdot|$ is $d$-dimensional volume. For any affine margin $\phi$ with $H=\{x:\phi(x)\ge0\}$, if $\sup_{x\in S}|\phi(x)-(\lambda_i(x)-b)|\le\eta\le(1-\delta)/(4m)$, then
$$
\frac{|(S\setminus K)\cap(H\mathbin{\triangle}C_i)|}{|S|}
\le 8m\eta(1-\delta)^{-d-1}\tau .
$$
In particular, $|(S\setminus K)\cap H|/|S|\le R_i+8m\eta(1-\delta)^{-d-1}\tau$. The affine margin may have any threshold satisfying the stated bound.

For the radial formula used to obtain this bound, let $F_j=\{\lambda_j=0\}\cap S$, let $\rho$ be the Minkowski gauge of $K-g$, and put $f_j(z)=\rho(z-g)-1$ and $w_j(z)=1-\rho(z-g)^{-d}$ on $F_j$. Each $f_j$ is continuous, convex and nonnegative, and $d(1-\delta)^d f_j\le w_j\le d f_j$. For a measurable $A\subset F_j$, the missing volume on rays from $g$ towards $A$ equals $(|S|/m)\int_A w_j\,d\mu_{F_j}$. In particular $\tau=m^{-1}\sum_j\int_{F_j} w_j\,d\mu_{F_j}$.
title: Uniform convex facet strips and missing volume of nearby simplex caps
